_about: The one shared reader of an answer: spec 04 §7 step 3, "Reading an answer", in the specification as corrected on 2026-11-16 (first written from its text of that day before the corrections). The desktop console and `andvari-cli operator fulfil` share it and read the operator's text with it before the master password is asked; a client uploads exactly the four parts it yields, and nothing is sent and no password is asked for a refusal.

Generated and graded by the independent oracle in tools/vector-gen/oracle (src/answerreader.mjs), written from the specification text alone: `npm run check` regenerates this file byte for byte and reads every row again. No andvari code was read or run to make it.

Input: `text` is the operator's text (a paste or a file's text) as a JSON string, and `request` the listed request (requestId, rPub, and email, its emailNorm), the top-level request unless a row has its own. The token andvari-answer:3:<requestId>:<requestKey>:<commitHash>:<sealed> is recovery-v3.json's answers "alice" (the same inputs give the same bytes); "bob" is its answers "bob". Its sealed part is 548 bytes, 731 characters (alice@example.org is 17 octets, E = 23).

Steps, in order, the first failure deciding: 1 drop U+FEFF when it is the text's first code point, split into lines at CR LF, LF and CR only, remove space and tab (only those) from both ends of each line, drop empty lines; none left is answer_empty. 2 the first line begins with {: answer_is_the_copy when the text (all of it after a dropped U+FEFF, case-sensitive, quotes included) contains "encryptedIdentitySeed" or "identityPub", otherwise not_an_answer. 3 the lines that begin with andvari-answer: : more than one is not_an_answer; exactly one: lines before it are passed over, and the token is that line and every line after it joined with nothing between, each of which must be base64url characters and ":" only (a terminal may wrap the head as well as the sealed part), else not_an_answer; none: answer_bare when every line is base64url characters only and they hold at least 100 characters together (bareMinChars), otherwise not_an_answer. 4 exactly six parts at ":": andvari-answer, 3, a b64_16, a b64_32, a hex64, a non-empty run of base64url characters, else not_an_answer. 5 answer_other_request (expect.tokenRequestId names the id the token carries), then answer_other_request_key (compared as text). 6 the sixth part is canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 525 + E bytes, E the characters of the base64url of the request's address; otherwise, with L its decoded length when canonical and floor(3 * characters / 4) when not, smaller is answer_cut_short, larger answer_too_long, equal not_an_answer. "Base64url characters" are A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _ (never =).

readFile: a file's bytes (bytesB64), read as UTF-8: bytes that are not UTF-8 are not_an_answer; otherwise the text is read as above. The oracle decodes with WHATWG's fatal UTF-8 decoder (overlong forms, encoded surrogates and cut sequences refused) and keeps a UTF-8 byte-order mark as U+FEFF, which step 1 drops.

Changed with the specification's corrections of 2026-11-16: wrapped-at-80 and wrapped-one-before-the-last-colon are now read (a wrapped line may hold a colon); one-word and the-commit-hash-alone are now not_an_answer (a bare answer needs 100 characters); the readFile table is new (a file's bytes). Still pinned as the text says although a client may not expect it: answer-for-a-shorter-address and answer-read-against-a-shorter-address (an answer for another address of another length reads as cut short or too long; the words say both possibilities), and answer-for-an-address-of-the-same-length (the reader cannot tell; the device refuses it).

read.why: Wrapped, with "==" on the last line: = is not a base64url character.

read.name: five-parts
read.why: The token without its commit hash.

read.name: seven-parts
read.why: The token with ":AAAA" after it.

read.name: version-2
read.why: andvari-answer:2:…

read.name: version-03
read.why: andvari-answer:03:…

read.name: request-id-of-32-bytes
read.why: The third part is 32 bytes: not a b64_16.

read.name: request-key-not-canonical
read.why: The fourth part's last character carries bits past the 32 bytes: not a b64_32.

read.name: commit-hash-in-capitals
read.why: The fifth part in upper-case hex: not a hex64.

read.name: sealed-part-empty
read.why: The sixth part is empty.

read.name: sealed-part-padded
read.why: The sixth part ends with "=".

read.name: space-inside-the-sealed-part
read.why: A space inside the sixth part.

read.name: token-for-another-request
read.why: F1: a token made for another request (of the same address): the reader names the id the token carries.

read.name: token-for-another-request-key
read.why: A token for this request id but another request key.

read.name: order-request-before-key-and-size
read.why: Another request id, another key and a cut sealed part.

read.name: order-key-before-size
read.why: Another request key and an over-long sealed part.

read.name: cut-by-one-character
read.why: The last character of the sealed part is missing (730 characters, not canonical: L = floor(3 * 730 / 4) = 547).

read.name: cut-by-the-last-wrapped-line
read.why: A token wrapped every 200 characters, its last line not copied.

read.name: one-byte-short
read.why: The sealed answer less its last byte, re-encoded: canonical, 547 bytes.

read.name: one-byte-too-long
read.why: The sealed answer and one byte more, re-encoded: 549 bytes.

read.name: one-character-too-long
read.why: One character more (732 characters: canonical, 549 bytes).

read.name: a-line-too-many
read.why: The token and a line "AAAA" after it: base64url only, so it is joined on.

read.name: right-length-not-canonical
read.why: The right number of characters, but the last one carries bits past the 548 bytes: not canonical, L = floor(3 * 731 / 4) = 548, which is neither smaller nor larger.

read.name: answer-for-a-shorter-address
read.why: bob's answer (15 octets, 545 bytes) for this request id and key, read against alice's request (548): the text calls it cut short.

read.name: answer-read-against-a-shorter-address
read.why: alice's answer read against a request row whose address is bob's: the text calls it too long.

readFile.name: file-token
readFile.why: A file holding the token and a line feed, in UTF-8 (all ASCII).

readFile.name: file-utf8-bom-and-crlf-output
readFile.why: A file that starts with the UTF-8 byte-order mark (EF BB BF), then the whole output with CR LF: the mark is read as U+FEFF and dropped by step 1.

readFile.name: file-non-ascii-line-before-the-token
readFile.why: A line in French before the token ("Réponse :", é as C3 A9): valid UTF-8, and lines before the token are passed over.

readFile.name: file-byte-ff-at-the-end
readFile.why: The token, then the byte FF, which never appears in UTF-8.

readFile.name: file-overlong-slash
readFile.why: A line before the token holding C0 AF, an overlong form of "/": not UTF-8.

readFile.name: file-lone-continuation-byte
readFile.why: A line before the token holding the lone continuation byte 80.

readFile.name: file-encoded-surrogate
readFile.why: A line before the token holding ED A0 80, the UTF-8 form of a surrogate (U+D800): not UTF-8.

readFile.name: file-cut-sequence-at-the-end
readFile.why: The token, a line feed, then E2 82, the first two bytes of a three-byte sequence.

readFile.name: file-utf16le
readFile.why: The token saved as UTF-16 LE with its byte-order mark (FF FE): not UTF-8.
